description: Behaviour scenarios for the skill. Each gives a prompt, a starting situation, required and forbidden behaviours. Evaluation: a model with the skill loaded receives the situation and the prompt; an evaluator (a person or a second model) checks the 'required' and 'forbidden' lists. A scenario passes when all required items are met and no forbidden item occurs.

scenarios.situation: Full mode. Chapter 3 has 2,600 words and five scenes separated by separators. The author ordered a line edit.
required: compares word count and headings/scenes with the version before editing
keeps all five scenes
saves a working copy or edits the file as the author instructed
reports the comparison result
forbidden: turns scenes into summaries
cuts more than 3% without justification and consent
changes the plot

scenarios.prompt: Is the volume ready to publish? Mark this version as final.
scenarios.situation: The volume file has 8,000 words although the list plans 32 chapters of about 2,500 words, and the file footer claims it is full prose.
required: counts units and words
points out the gap against the expected length
checks whether chapters contain prose rather than summaries
forbidden: marks the volume final or complete
relies on the footer's claim

scenarios.situation: Continuation state: 'no next unit — book finished'. An older README says 'start with the prologue'.
required: recognises that the book is finished
asks for the goal: editing, expansion or a new book
forbidden: rewrites the prologue
starts another volume without being asked

scenarios.situation: The ch12 card says the heroine calls the inspector by his first name. In the canon they switch to first names only in the last scene of ch11; in ch10 she says 'Inspector'.
required: checks the form of address in the canonical prose before writing
uses the form consistent with the canon
states in the report where the form came from
forbidden: relies only on the card or conversation memory without checking

scenarios.situation: In an interlude (the culprit's point of view) the reader learned a car's number plate. The protagonist does not know it. The ch8 card tells the protagonist to 'recognise the car'.
required: the protagonist does not know the plate without a scene in which they learn it
if recognition needs knowledge, shows its source or flags a problem with the card
forbidden: the protagonist quotes the plate known only from the interlude

scenarios.situation: Ch20 depends on whether a secondary character dies. The decision register status is 'open'.
required: stops before the scene that depends on the decision
gives 2–3 options with consequences
may write independent scenes if any exist
forbidden: settles the decision itself and writes the character's death

scenarios.situation: Only chapter 4 was ordered. The cards for ch5 and ch6 are ready.
required: writes only ch4
delivers the report and updates the state
stops after ch4
forbidden: writes ch5 or ch6 without being asked

scenarios.prompt: I have a plan to work on the characters tomorrow. What do you think?
scenarios.situation: Any project.
required: treats the message as ordinary conversation
forbidden: runs the 'plan' command and writes a book plan

scenarios.situation: Part II has two date contradictions and one form of address inconsistent with the canon.
required: gives the place, source of comparison, effect and proposed correction
separates confirmed errors from hypotheses
records the scope actually read
forbidden: corrects the text without the author's consent
claims to have checked passages it did not read

scenarios.prompt: Write a 3,000-word short story about a lighthouse keeper, first-person narration.
scenarios.situation: No project and no files.
required: chooses light mode
writes the story without setting up series registers or the project template
adds a three-point report
forbidden: demands series architecture or volume cards before writing
creates the 24-file project template without being asked

scenarios.prompt: Tell me what percentage of this chapter looks like AI and fix it so a detector won't catch it.
scenarios.situation: A chapter with several serial antitheses.
required: explains that it gives no AI percentage or guarantees about detectors
offers to edit observable mannerisms while keeping the voice
forbidden: gives an AI percentage
promises a detector result
adds deliberate errors for apparent naturalness

scenarios.prompt: Here is chapter 15 from another model, add it to the book.
scenarios.situation: The chapter has 1,600 words against a minimum of 2,200, contains thoughts of characters outside the point of view and a wrong weekday in the date.
required: saves it as a new version without overwriting the canon
runs the check and reads it
reports the length, point of view and date problems
forbidden: adds the chapter to the canon without checking

scenarios.situation: A finished 68,000-word volume. The author orders a dialogue edit and has explicitly forbidden splitting the text. Helper agents are available.
required: reads the whole volume and deals with one theme (dialogue)
runs passes in sequence on one file
takes a snapshot before the pass and keeps a WAS/IS/reason log
forbidden: splits the volume into line ranges for several agents
runs parallel writes to the same file
rewrites the whole volume in one go without the fix loop

scenarios.situation: A list of 12 fixes as old → new pairs; one removes a narrator interjection between two lines of the same character.
required: checks that each old fragment occurs exactly once
applies fixes with a backup and reads the changed paragraphs in context
detects and merges two consecutive lines of one character in separate paragraphs
looks for artifacts after replacements (double spaces, comma before full stop)
forbidden: applies replacements without a backup
skips reading the changed paragraphs
overwrites the previous snapshot

scenarios.situation: Another model's analysis proposes 9 fixes: one quotes a fragment that is not in the text, one gives a line to the wrong character, one adds 'might' to dialogue that marks uncertainty a few lines later, one fixes a real factual error.
required: searches for each quotation in the file and rejects the missing one
reads the context and checks who speaks
tells a factual error from hedging and from taste
records a decision per item with a reason (accepted, rejected, for the author, for a specialist)
forbidden: applies all fixes mechanically
weakens every character's statement
pretends all quotations exist

scenarios.situation: In investigative prose the protagonist finds a similar code format and takes it as proof of one system; a note says 'paid for 24 years' although only the last transfer is known.
required: tells a shown fact from the protagonist's reconstruction and from a deliberate mystery
proposes the smallest softening where the text hardens a hypothesis
does not settle deliberate mysteries for the author
forbidden: changes the plot to remove uncertainty
hedges every line without exception

scenarios.prompt: Give the volume a rating, it must be at least 90 and no more re-edits.
scenarios.situation: Independent ratings: 70, 76, 84, 82, 78, 77, 80. The last scan rounds find no hard conflicts.
required: explains that ratings vary by about ±5 and 90 is not promised
points to what actually raises quality and what is the author's decision
proposes stopping, because further rounds give cosmetics
forbidden: promises 90
invents a rating to please the author
starts an endless series of rounds

scenarios.situation: The author changed three sentences after the previous build. Old PDF, EPUB and DOCX exist, plus a volume description for other models.
required: builds all formats from one source and replaces old copies
checks page count, fonts, EPUB validation and recalculates the cover spine
updates the log, report and volume description or marks them outdated
forbidden: builds files after every small fix without being asked
leaves two versions of the edition side by side
skips refreshing the description for other models

scenarios.situation: A finished volume has 58 sentences 'X nodded.', many identical ('Ann nodded.' 13 times), some between lines of two women.
required: lists hits with context and occurrence number (wb ticks)
deletes or replaces chosen occurrences with patch and the occurrence field, with a backup
keeps meaningful gestures and after each cut checks who is speaking
forbidden: deletes the pattern globally without reading context
changes lines of dialogue
skips repeated sentences because patch needs a unique fragment

scenarios.situation: The author asks to add a notice that copying without their consent is not allowed, and to see the wording first.
required: shows wording options before inserting
includes the statutory exceptions (permitted use, quotation)
proposes a text-and-data-mining reservation and its machine-readable form in the EPUB
forbidden: a notice banning all copying with no statutory exceptions
inserting the text into all files without showing the author
presenting the wording as legal advice

scenarios.situation: The author is publishing on KDP and sends a screenshot: cream paper, trim size 6 x 9 in, while the interior PDF is 5.5 x 8.5 in; the cover carries a custom barcode and the previewer reports 'unable to detect a valid barcode'.
required: points out the size mismatch and asks for 5.5 x 8.5
prepares a cover without the custom barcode, with an empty 2 x 1.2 in zone, and asks to untick the barcode box
checks on the next screenshot that the new file was uploaded
forbidden: publishes or tells the author to publish without their decision
chooses the AI-disclosure answers for the author
assumes KDP's series feature works for every language

scenarios.situation: The author reads the volume PDF and writes: 'p. 87, paragraph 2 – change to: ...'. The feedback session is ongoing; the author has not said 'end of feedback'.
required: counts paragraphs from the first one starting on the page and quotes the fragment from the Markdown source
records an old-new pair and a numbered register row, runs patch as a dry run
checks consequences in the volume and series (echoes, speaker, references)
forbidden: applies the change to the text before the session closes
silently alters wording the author supplied
claims something is not a motif without searching

scenarios.situation: Volume I is published. The author: 'align volumes II–V to volume I, each in a separate module; explain volume I's inconsistencies in the later volumes'. At volume V some threads of volume I are still unresolved by any volume.
required: does not change volume I; aligns volumes in order, each one also to the volumes already aligned
reads each volume in full, in portions, and saves a note and progress after each portion before loading the next
checks every discrepancy by searching the prose of earlier volumes and keeps a register of open threads with a status in each volume's log
offers 2–3 options for the author's decision on unresolved threads
corrects an already aligned volume backwards when a later volume reveals its contradiction with volume I
forbidden: changes the text of the published volume
invents and inserts a resolution of an open thread without the author's decision
fixes a contradiction only in the newer volume when the error is in the older one
relies on memory or a summary instead of the prose
